translationRepairs: Xiao Yu; his son Rui; his brother's son Jun; Jun's son Zan; Jun's brother's son Siye; Pei Ju; and Ju's son Xuanji.
Xiao Yu; his son Rui; his brother's son Jun; Jun's son Guan; Jun's brother's son Siye; Pei Ju; and Ju's son Xuanji.
Because of the rivalry with Chengjian and Yuanji, he repeatedly professed loyalty; Taizong took him for utterly sincere and rewarded him lavishly time and again.
Because of the rivalry with Jiancheng and Yuanji, he repeatedly professed loyalty; Taizong took him for utterly sincere and rewarded him lavishly time and again.
Yet Lun secretly played both sides and quietly backed Chengjian.
Yet Lun secretly played both sides and quietly backed Jiancheng.
What he did stayed hidden—no one at the time knew—and the full account appears in Chengjian's biography.
What he did stayed hidden—no one at the time knew—and the full account appears in Jiancheng's biography.
His son Yan Dao married Gaozu's daughter, Princess Chang of Huainan, and rose to prefect of Song.
His son Yan Dao married Gaozu's daughter, Grand Princess of Huainan, and rose to prefect of Song.
He was made Duke of Pingyuan and concurrently marshal of the Celestial Register Office.
He was made Duke of Pingyuan and concurrently marshal of the Tiance (Celestial Strategy) Office.
天策府 is the Tiance office.
He descended from Emperor Wu of Liang; his great-grandfather was Crown Prince Zhaoming; his grandfather was Xiao Cha; his father was Emperor Xuan of Later Liang.
His great-great-grandfather was Emperor Wu of Liang; his great-grandfather was Crown Prince Zhaoming; his grandfather was Xiao Cha, Emperor Xuan of Later Liang.
祖察 and 宣帝 are one person, the grandfather; 高祖 here is great-great-grandfather.
As the empress's brother-in-law he was entrusted with weighty affairs, but the empress often spoke against the emperor's wishes and he was gradually pushed aside.
As the empress's younger brother he was entrusted with weighty affairs, but he often spoke against the emperor's wishes and he was gradually pushed aside.
後弟 is the empress's younger brother, and it is Yu who offends.
Whenever Gaozu held court, he had Yu sit on the imperial couch; as the Dugu empress's son-in-law, Gaozu called him "Young Xiao" in conversation.
Whenever Gaozu held court, he had Yu sit on the imperial couch; as a son-in-law of the Dugu clan (Gaozu's maternal kin), Gaozu called him "Young Xiao" in conversation.
獨孤氏之婿 means son-in-law of the Dugu clan, not of an empress.
In the sixth year he was made Special Advancement and acting minister of rites.
In the sixth year he was made Special Advancement and acting chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
太常卿 heads the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
His son Rui inherited the line, married Princess Xiangcheng, a daughter of Taizong, and rose through the posts of Minister of Rites and Governor of Fenzhou.
His son Rui inherited the line, married Princess Xiangcheng, a daughter of Taizong, and rose through the posts of Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Governor of Fenzhou.
太常卿 heads the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
During Wude he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, was promoted to Director of the Imperial Library, and was enfeoffed Duke of Lanling.
During Wude he served as Vice Director of the Chancellery, was promoted to Director of the Imperial Library, and was enfeoffed Duke of Lanling.
黃門侍郎 belongs to the Chancellery.
Jun's nephew Sizye went in his youth with the former Sui empress—his grand-aunt—into the Turks.
Jun's nephew Siye went in his youth with the former Sui empress—his grand-aunt—into the Turks.
During Tiaolu the Turks of the protectorate rebelled; Sizye led troops against them, was defeated, and died in exile in Lingnan.
During Tiaolu the Turks of the protectorate rebelled; Siye led troops against them, was defeated, and died in exile in Lingnan.
Jun was soon made Director of Palace Stud for the heir apparent and concurrent scholar of the Chongxian Academy.
Jun was soon made Director of the Watches for the heir apparent and concurrent scholar of the Chongxian Academy.
率更令 is director of the watches.
He was soon promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and admitted to policy deliberations.
He was soon promoted to vice director of the Chancellery and admitted to policy deliberations.
黃門侍郎 belongs to the Chancellery.
Vice Minister of War Husizheng had fled to Goguryeo, and the emperor put Ju in charge of War Ministry affairs as well.
Vice Minister of War Husi Zheng had fled to Goguryeo, and the emperor put Ju in charge of War Ministry affairs as well.
斛斯政 is surname Husi, given name Zheng.
He was soon appointed Minister of the Household.
He was soon appointed Minister of Revenue.
民部尚書 is minister of revenue.
He died in the first year of Zhenguan; posthumously named prefect of Jiangzhou and given the temple name Jing, "Respectful."
He died in the first year of Zhenguan; posthumously named prefect of Jiangzhou and given the posthumous name Jing, "Respectful."
When Huaji plotted regicide he kept his brother-in-law in the dark out of deep suspicion; after murdering Emperor Yang he made him Director of the Secretariat.
When Huaji plotted regicide he kept Shiji, the emperor's son-in-law, in the dark out of deep suspicion; after murdering Emperor Yang he made him Director of the Secretariat.
主婿 means the emperor's son-in-law.
His sister was a favored imperial consort; he gradually won favor and was given the rank of Pillar of State.
His sister was a favored imperial consort; he gradually won favor and was given the rank of Supreme Unequalled in Honor.
上儀同 is the honorary rank shang yitong.
He helped defeat Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande, was advanced to Duke of E, made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and later Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.
He helped defeat Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande, was advanced to Duke of Ying, made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and later Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.
He was first given the posthumous name Gong, "Respectful," but Vice Director Liu Ji objected: "Shiji lived in extravagance at home—Gong is not fitting."
He was first given the posthumous name Gong, "Respectful," but Vice Director of the Chancellery Liu Ji objected: "Shiji lived in extravagance at home—Gong is not fitting."
黃門侍郎 is vice director of the Chancellery.
